In [[geometric group theory]] and [[dynamical systems]] the '''iterated monodromy group''' of a [[covering map]] is a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] describing the [[monodromy action]] of the [[fundamental group]] on all [[iteration]]s of the covering. A single covering map between spaces is therefore used to create a tower of coverings, by placing the covering over itself repeatedly. In terms of the [[Galois theory of covering spaces]], this construction on spaces is expected to correspond to a construction on groups. The iterated monodromy group provides this construction, and it is applied to encode the combinatorics and [[symbolic dynamics]] of the covering, and provide examples of [[self-similar group]]s.

==Definition==

The '''iterated monodromy group''' of ''f'' is the following [[quotient group]]:
:<math>\mathrm{IMG}f := \frac{\pi_1 (X, t)}{\bigcap_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathrm{Ker}\,\digamma^n}</math>

where :

*<math>f:X_1\rightarrow X</math> is a [[covering map|covering]] of a [[Connected space#Path connectedness|path-connected]] and [[Connected space#Local connectedness|locally path-connected]] topological space ''X'' by its subset <math>X_1</math>, 
* <math>\pi_1 (X, t)</math> is the [[fundamental group]] of ''X'' and
* <math>\digamma :\pi_1 (X, t)\rightarrow \mathrm{Sym}\,f^{-1}(t)</math> is the [[monodromy group|monodromy action]] for ''f''.
* <math>\digamma^n:\pi_1 (X, t)\rightarrow \mathrm{Sym}\,f^{-n}(t)</math> is the monodromy action of the <math>n^\mathrm{th}</math> iteration of ''f'', <math>\forall n\in\mathbb{N}_0</math>.

==Action==
The iterated monodromy group acts by [[automorphisms|automorphism]] on the [[Tree (graph theory)|rooted tree]] of preimages
:<math>T_f := \bigsqcup_{n\ge 0}f^{-n}(t),</math>
where a vertex <math>z\in f^{-n}(t)</math> is connected by an edge with <math>f(z)\in f^{-(n-1)}(t)</math>.

==Examples==

===Iterated monodromy groups of rational functions===
Let :
* ''f'' be a complex [[rational function]] 
* <math>P_f</math> be the union of [[Orbit (dynamics)|forward orbits]] of its [[Critical point (mathematics)|critical points]] (the [[post-critical set]]).

If <math>P_f</math> is finite (or has a finite set of [[accumulation point]]s), then the iterated monodromy group of ''f'' is the iterated monodromy group of the covering <math>f:\hat C\setminus f^{-1}(P_f)\rightarrow \hat C\setminus P_f</math>, where <math>\hat C</math> is the [[Riemann sphere]].

Iterated monodromy groups of rational functions usually have exotic properties from the point of view of classical group theory. Most of them are infinitely presented, many have [[intermediate growth]].

==== IMG of polynomials====

The [[Basilica group]] is the iterated monodromy group of the polynomial <math>z^2 - 1</math>
